name: Reaction–Diffusion (Gray–Scott model)
subtitle: Two chemicals feeding and consuming each other bloom into coral
rule: Every cell holds two chemicals — one is constantly fed in, the other eats it to make more of itself — and both endlessly leak into neighboring cells at different speeds.
detail: Because the eater diffuses more slowly than its food, a seeded spot can't just spread evenly: its edge stays fed while its middle starves, so blobs stretch, split, and branch. Watch a single injected droplet undergo mitosis-like division, then knit into coral fingers and labyrinth walls that negotiate their spacing with their neighbors. The final maze is never designed anywhere — it is just the standing truce between feeding, eating, and leaking.
interaction: Click or drag to inject a droplet of catalyst and watch it divide and bloom.
issues: resize() throws TypeError after destroy(): destroy() nulls off/offCtx, and a subsequent resize() with changed client dimensions hits `off.width = gw` on null (verified by test — a lingering window-resize listener would crash the page). Fixed with a one-line guard: `if (!w || !h || !off) return;` at the top of resize().

name: Dendritic Growth
subtitle: Diffusion-limited aggregation
rule: Particles wander randomly until they touch the frozen cluster, and the instant they touch, they freeze in place too.
detail: Random walkers almost never reach the deep fjords between branches — they get caught by the tips first — so growth amplifies every bump into a branch, and branches into sub-branches, producing a fractal crystal no one designed. Cells are tinted by the moment they froze: the oldest core fades to deep blue while the actively growing tips burn cyan-white, so you can watch the growth front glow as it creeps outward. Faint blue specks are the live walkers still diffusing.
interaction: Click or drag to plant a new frost seed for the walkers to crystallize around.

name: Particle Life
subtitle: Asymmetric attraction among six species
rule: Every particle shoves away anything that gets too close, then drifts toward or away from nearby particles according to a lopsided table of attractions between its species and theirs.
detail: Because the attraction matrix is asymmetric — red may chase green while green flees red — the swarm never settles into a static crystal; instead it self-assembles into chasing chains, orbiting cells, and membrane-like clusters that continually digest one another. Watch for pursuit trains where one color perpetually hunts another, and for stable "molecules" where mutual short-range repulsion balances long-range pull. Every reseed rolls a new matrix, so the ecosystem's whole character changes.
interaction: Click or drag to blast nearby particles outward with a swirl.
issues: Degenerate-grid double counting: in resize(), `rMax = Math.max(24, Math.min(rMax, W/3, H/3))` lets the 24px floor override the W/3,H/3 clamp on canvases under 72px in a dimension, so gw or gh can drop below 3. The wrapped neighbor scan `(cx + ox + gw) % gw` then visits the same cell 2-3 times per axis, counting every pairwise force up to 9x — wrong physics (though bounded, no NaN/crash), and it contradicted the code's own 'grid >= 3x3' comment. Fixed minimally in step() by shrinking the offset range when a grid dimension is < 3 (`oxMax = gw > 2 ? 1 : gw - 2`, same for gh) so each cell is visited exactly once.

name: Spiral Waves
subtitle: Cyclic cellular automaton
rule: Each cell holds one of 14 colors arranged in a cycle, and it advances to the next color only when at least one of its eight neighbors already shows that next color.
detail: From pure random noise, this one-line rule first carves out blotchy debris, then closed loops of color-chasing-color that wind into rotating spiral galaxies. Each spiral turns once every 14 ticks, and competing spirals fight for territory along shearing wavefronts until a few dominant cores own the whole field. Watch the first few seconds closely — the transition from static to spirals is the entire phenomenon, and a click drops fresh rings of state that either bloom into a new spiral or get devoured by an established one.
interaction: Click or drag to seed rings of color that nucleate new spirals.

name: Strange Attractor (Clifford / de Jong map)
subtitle: Millions of hops of one point, condensing into glowing filaments
rule: A single point hops forever by one fixed rule — its next position is a sine-and-cosine fold of its current one — and every pixel it lands on gets one count brighter.
detail: The fold stretches and creases the plane over and over, so the point never repeats yet never escapes; the places it revisits most often trace the attractor's dense ridges. Nothing is drawn directly — the image is a log-scaled histogram of visits, so it starts as faint dust and sharpens into indigo-to-cyan filaments as counts accumulate over seconds. Watch how brightness reveals structure at every zoom level: folds within folds, the fingerprint of chaos with fractal fine grain.
interaction: Click or drag to bend the map's four parameters toward the pointer — the image resets and re-condenses into a new shape.

name: Slime Mold
subtitle: Physarum transport network
rule: Each of 28,000 agents sniffs the trail chemical at three points ahead, turns toward the strongest scent, steps forward, and deposits more trail where it lands.
detail: Because agents both follow and reinforce trails, faint paths either evaporate or snowball into highways — the same positive feedback a real slime mold uses to link food sources. Watch the early haze condense into a glowing, branching vein network whose junctions migrate while redundant loops starve and vanish. Each reseed re-rolls the sensing angles and distances, so the networks range from tight lace to broad braided rivers.
interaction: Click or drag to drop a chemical blob — nearby agents swarm toward it.
